assets: the tower/gate verdict on a commit, the only proof the merge queue takes
the gate's rules, scripts and workflows
boundaries: a pull request's code (a session's, or a fork's) and the GitHub-hosted runner that judges it
the pull request run and the merge queue run that reuses its tests' verdict
the staged workflows of this tree and the ones the owner installs in .github/workflows

threats.statement: A run that did not judge the commit, such as a fork's run or a run of another head, passes its green verdict off as the queue commit's; or a tower/gate status is posted on a commit by a credential other than the gate's own job. The ruleset binds each required check to the GitHub Actions app (integration 15368), so a status of that name from a session's credential (verify-commit without --no-post) or any other writer does not count. Residual: the binding is staged in .github/rulesets/main.json and holds once the owner applies it to the live ruleset (VULN-gate-check-source stays open until then).

A pull request edits the gate itself (its scripts, its rules, its registry keys, the verifier or a workflow) so that its own change passes. The gate's files (GATE_FILE: the stages, the structure and commit checks, config/registry/gate/, scripts/verify-commit) ask a decision, and the pinned job of tower/gate judges a change to them with the base's gate: the base's gate_pin.py puts the base's gate files back in the checkout and the plan's stages run there (D-070 on GitHub). Residual: the pinned job is staged in services/runner/github/tower-gate.yml and holds once the owner installs it (VULN-gate-judged-by-own-head stays open until then); the workflow itself is the owner's to change (D-087), and the head's tests run the head's code, as code under test.

A dependency or tool the gate runs is swapped for a malicious version between two runs. Residual: the workflow's actions are pinned by a tag, not a commit; the supply measure counts them unpinned and no check refuses one.
A pushed history is rewritten so that what merged is not what was judged.
A merge cannot be traced to the verdict and the commit that justified it.

A secret committed in a change reaches the public repository and its history. Residual: the gate sees a pushed commit, already public on its branch; the earlier barrier is the pre-push scan, which runs on the client and is skipped by a push that bypasses the hook.

A change floods the queue or hangs the gate, so no other change lands. Residual: the 60 s requirement is a target, not a bound; a hung run is stopped by the job's timeout and the queue's check timeout.

The ruleset requires no approving review (D-055), so any account that may push a branch and enqueue it lands whatever passes the gate's checks; the checks, not a person, are the whole barrier. Residual: a change that is malicious but passes every rule is not caught.

findings.finding: The ruleset requires tower/gate by context only (no source app), and scripts/verify-commit posts that status with the session's own credential when run without --no-post, so a status from any writer of statuses satisfies the queue; neither mitigation listed refuses that.
findings.reason: VULN-gate-check-source; .github/rulesets/main.json binds tower/gate and web to the GitHub Actions app (integration_id 15368) and security.test.sh refuses a required check without it; the owner applies it to ruleset 27250343, and the VULN is fixed on that date.

findings.finding: The listed rules (allowed workflows, workflows refused, structure check) run from the head under judgment: the GitHub job does not use the base-pinned gate of D-070, so a change that rewrites the gate judges itself.
findings.reason: VULN-gate-judged-by-own-head; gate_pin.py overlay and verify-commit --stages-only (gate-pin and verify-commit tests), run by the pinned job staged in services/runner/github/tower-gate.yml (D-087: the owner installs it, after gate_pin.py overlay is on main, since the job runs the base's copy); the VULN is fixed on the date it is installed.

findings.finding: STD-commit-check-gate-errors, the rule that asks a decision of a gate change, was missing from the gate's own tampering threat.
The third-party actions of tower-gate.yml are pinned by tag (v4), not commit; supply.py counts them unpinned and refuses nothing.
findings.reason: residual added; the actions are GitHub's own, the party that already runs the runner and the ruleset.

findings.finding: The secret scans run after the push, when the commit is already public on its branch.
findings.reason: residual added; the pre-push scan (local-checks) named as the earlier, client-side barrier.

findings.finding: REQ-gate-60s is a target, not a mitigation of a hung or flooding change.
findings.reason: the job timeout (tower-gate.yml) and the queue's check timeout (rulesets/main.json) added; residual stated.

findings.finding: The residual is honest; together with the two open findings the checks are not yet the barrier the statement says they are.
findings.reason: kept as written; it holds once the two VULNs are fixed.
